title: Dermatomes, levels, and the viscera
objective: Explain dermatomes and that visceral organs map to particular spinal levels, including the gut and pancreas.

steps.title: Each level owns a strip of skin
steps.body: A **[[dermatome]]** is the patch of skin whose sensation is carried by one spinal segment. Stack the segments and the body's surface is mapped level by level. This is why a pinched root causes numbness in a predictable band — the segment predicts the territory.

steps.title: Viscera map to levels too
steps.body: Internal organs also connect to particular spinal levels. Spinal ([[DRG]]) afferents from abdominal organs largely enter at **thoracic and upper-lumbar** levels (via splanchnic nerves), with pelvic organs adding **lumbosacral** input. This is partly why visceral pain is felt in broad, referred regions rather than a sharp spot.

flag.note: Exact level ranges vary by organ and species; treat specific numbers as approximate and confirm for the pancreas with the lab/primary literature.

steps.prompt: Why is visceral pain usually felt as a vague, broad region rather than a precise point?
options: Visceral afferents are sparse and converge onto spinal levels shared with skin, so the brain localizes them poorly
Only the vagus carries it, and the vagus can't localize
steps.explanation: Sparse visceral innervation plus convergence onto the same dorsal-horn levels as somatic input makes precise localization impossible — the basis of referred pain.

steps.setup: For your pancreas project, you need the DRG levels whose neurons innervate the pancreas.
steps.prompt: What's the right way to pin those down?
options: Assume they're the same as the colon
Retrograde-label from the pancreas and see which DRG light up, and check the lab's primary literature — don't guess exact levels
Levels don't matter for viral injection
steps.reveal: Retrograde labeling from the organ reveals the actual levels empirically (C4), rather than assuming. Pancreatic spinal afferents are generally thoracic/splanchnic, but confirm the specific levels for your line and prep before planning injections.

reviewNotes: Confidence 'medium' due to organ/species level variation; flagged. Hands off to A-track interoception and the capstone.
